steps.body: With several measurements, comparing means ranking: scan every number before naming the longest or the shortest.
steps.narration: With several measurements, comparing means ranking: scan every number before naming the longest or the shortest.

widget.prompt: Two of the four items, aligned: which of these two is longer?
widget.unalignedFeedback: Looks can trick you — line the starting ends up first.
widget.missFeedback: Now the starts are lined up — check the far ends again: the one reaching farther is longer.
widget.successFeedback: Same start makes the compare fair — the bottom ribbon really does reach farther.

predict.prompt: An item is longer than TWO others in a set of four. Is it the longest?
predict.reveal: Beating some is not beating all; the crown needs every comparison.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2p compare two.
invariants: Lengths compare only from a shared start, join by placing end to end, and split so the parts rebuild the whole exactly for g2p compare two.
misconceptions: Comparing unaligned ends, reading a ruler's end mark as a length, or letting a total drift from the sum of its parts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What would have to change about the pieces for the total or the gap to come out differently?

widget.prompt: The ribbon is 10 inches. The shoelace is 15 inches. The bookmark is 18 inches. The straw is 7 inches. Which is the longest?

options.label: bookmark
options.feedback: Correct — at 18 inches the bookmark outreaches every other item on the list.

options.label: ribbon
options.feedback: The ribbon measures 10 inches — compare all four numbers before crowning the longest.

options.label: shoelace
options.feedback: At 15 inches the shoelace sits in the middle of the pack, not at the longest end.

options.label: straw
options.feedback: The straw's 7 inches is the wrong extreme — that is nearer the shortest.

commonErrors.feedback: That joined the two lengths — "how much longer" wants the gap between them, found by subtracting.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the lengths up: same starting point, then read what the ends say — joins add, gaps subtract.
